title: observability: add token-level KV cost/latency dashboard, refine alerts and tracing labels
author: Aisha Khan
description: Motivation: Operators need a single-pane view for token-level cost and latency with KV cache visibility to diagnose regressions and optimize batching/quantization choices. This PR adds a token-level KV dashboard, enriches tracing with KV hit/miss tags, and tightens alerting criteria to reduce noisy pages. Changes are backward-compatible and behind a feature flag (obs.token_kv_dashboard.enabled). Checklist: - [x] Add Grafana dashboard JSON with panels for token cost, per-token latency distribution (P50/P90/P99), KV hit/miss rate, KV-induced latency heatmap - [x] Expose new metrics: redwood.kv.cache_hits, redwood.kv.cache_misses, redwood.kv.latency_bucket - [x] Add tracing tags: kv_hit, kv_latency_ms, batch_size - [x] Create alert rules: KV miss rate > 5% (5m), token P99 latency > 1200ms (5m), cost anomaly guardrail (7d rolling) - [x] Unit & integration tests for metric emission and alert rule templates - [x] Docs: short runbook + dashboard walkthrough What I changed (high-level): - telemetry/dashboards/token_kv_dashboard.json: new Grafana dashboard with 8 panels (cost breakdown, latency percentiles, KV hit/miss, KV latency heatmap, per-model breakdown, per-region trend, trace-sample links). - telemetry/alerts/token_kv_alert_rules.yaml: new alertgroup with tuned thresholds and notification routing (pager for production, slack for staging). - runtime/metrics/kv_metrics.go: instrument KV hits/misses and latency histograms. - runtime/tracing/span_tags.go: add kv_hit and kv_latency_ms tags and hook into sampled spans only to control volume. - docs/observability/token_kv_dashboard.md: usage, troubleshooting, and how to interpret token-cost arithmetic. - .github/workflows/observability.yml: add an integration job that runs the dashboard generation + lint for alert rules. Notes on rollout: feature flag enabled for a small percentage of hosts initially; alerts default to warning for staging. See linked linear tasks for the rollout plan. CI: initial run flagged a flaky integration test (observability_integration::dashboard_render_test) which was caused by a timing assumption in the test harness; test was made time-tolerant and re-run. All checks passed on the final run. Backwards compatibility: metrics additions are additive and do not change existing metric names. No schema-breaking changes. Related: ENG-9123 (dashboard rollout), ENG-9210 (kv-metrics perf), SUP-321 (customer incident that motivated alert tuning).

review_comments: Carlos Mendez (review): Please add pagination on the dashboard variables when there are >200 models to avoid UI blowup. Also ask that alert notifications include the model label in the payload.
Aisha Khan (author): Added model pagination to dashboard templating and included model label in the pager payload. Updated alert rule annotations to include {{ $labels.model }}.
Sophie Turner (review): The KV latency histogram uses 10ms buckets — can we make that configurable? Suggest exposing a config value and defaulting to the current buckets.
Aisha Khan (author): Made bucket boundaries configurable via telemetry.kv_latency_buckets; kept default to 10ms buckets for now and documented in the runbook.
Jae Park (review): Observability integration test was failing intermittently in my local runs. After your fix runs green in CI. Approving on green.
Carlos Mendez (approve): LGTM after changes; integrated alert routing looks sane.
discussion_threads: Thread: alert thresholds and noise - agreed to start conservative and iterate based on 2 weeks of telemetry
Thread: trace sampling - agreed to sample 1% of requests with kv tags for production; 10% in staging
Thread: rollout plan - feature flag, 5% hosts -> 25% -> 100% with post-rollout validation queries
release_notes: Add token-level KV cost & latency Grafana dashboard; new KV metrics (redwood.kv.cache_hits, redwood.kv.cache_misses, redwood.kv.latency_bucket); tuned alerts for KV miss-rate and token P99 latency. Backwards-compatible additions only.
notes_for_ops: Feature flag: obs.token_kv_dashboard.enabled=false by default. To enable: set feature flag and run telemetry/dashboard sync. Alerts will start as WARN in staging; promote to pager after 2 weeks if stable. If paging spikes, disable the token_kv alertgroup via the alertmanager UI and investigate KV miss rate per model.
testing_summary: Unit tests added for metrics emission; integration test simulates KV hit/miss traffic and verifies dashboard panels render without timing assumptions. CI initially failed due to a brittle timing assertion; fixed and re-run successfully.
notes: This PR is part of the broader token-level observability effort (see many prior PRs). It focuses on KV-specific telemetry and should reduce time-to-detect for cache-related regressions by surfacing both cost and latency per-token metrics.
